findings.claim: Backpressure is no longer respected: the return value of `writer.write()` is ignored and the loop never waits for a `drain` event
findings.rationale: `pipeline()` (removed here) handled backpressure automatically. With the manual loop, the web stream is drained as fast as `reader.read()` resolves and every chunk is pushed into the Node writable regardless of its high-water mark. For large or slow-consuming Lambda response streams this buffers the whole body in memory. Fix: await a `drain` promise when `write()` returns `false`. High confidence this is a real regression.

findings.claim: No error handling: if `reader.read()` rejects or the writer emits `error`, the reader is never cancelled and `writer.end()` is never called
findings.rationale: `pipeline()` previously guaranteed cleanup — destroying the destination and cancelling the source on failure, and propagating writer errors as a rejection. Now an exception from `reader.read()` propagates out with `writer.end()` skipped, leaving the Lambda response stream open (invocation can hang until timeout) and the web-stream reader un-cancelled. Also, no `error` listener is attached to `writer`, so a writer error becomes an unhandled 'error' event that can crash the process instead of rejecting this promise. High confidence.

findings.claim: The returned promise resolves immediately after `writer.end()` instead of waiting for the stream to finish flushing
findings.rationale: `pipeline()` resolved only after the destination emitted `finish`. Now `end()` is fire-and-forget, so `streamToNodeStream()` resolves while data may still be buffered. A caller awaiting this before completing the Lambda handler may terminate the response early or miss a late write error. Should await `finished(writer)` or the `end()` callback. Fairly high confidence.

findings.claim: The `pipeline` import may now be unused after removing the only call site
findings.rationale: This hunk removes the sole `pipeline(...)` usage shown. The hunk header implies one line was already removed earlier (likely the import), but if the `stream/promises` import remains it will fail builds with `noUnusedLocals`/lint. Low confidence — worth verifying.
